question: Should OpenClaw support a production current-DM recovery lifecycle, and if so should it remain Telegram-extension-owned rather than become a public plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The branch adds a new opt-in recovery capability with persistence, freshness, and scheduling dependencies but does not provide the host lifecycle that enables it; choosing its supported boundary and rollout is a product and ownership decision.

options.title: Keep it extension-owned
options.body: Move the Telegram-specific markers and recovery interfaces out of the public SDK, define the Telegram host lifecycle, and add live proof before considering a narrow follow-up.

options.title: Approve a generic SDK capability
options.body: Explicitly define a channel-neutral delivery-observation contract, its compatibility guarantees, and which channel owners may depend on it before retaining public SDK exports.

options.title: Pause the recovery feature
options.body: Retain no preparatory public surface until a maintainer sponsors a concrete product and rollout direction.

recommendation.title: Keep it extension-owned
recommendation.body: Move the Telegram-specific markers and recovery interfaces out of the public SDK, define the Telegram host lifecycle, and add live proof before considering a narrow follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current design and can incorporate an explicit owner decision, though main-history ownership could not be established from the available review environment.
